difficulty.notes: Single-line minified webpack bundle (4f4f4b5.js). The interceptor x sets reqId, plat, from, httpsStatus on the same request (sibling fields, not separate functions). uuid.v1 is module 113 in shared chunk 8dcf22e.js and is scored as a 0.5 core utility together with its rng/stringify helpers. Search trigger/call-site functions and the response-side callback are 0.2 path roles. There is no valid 0.7 nested helper because x calls the generic uuid library and binds reqId inline. GA/googletagmanager/bdstatic are analytics noise.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The request interceptor x that generates a uuid and binds it to t.data.reqId; not the search handler, the uuid lib, or result formatters. The 0.7 nested-helper tier is intentionally empty because the reqId-specific binding happens inline in x.

behavior_category.subtype: v1 uuid reqId attached by an axios request interceptor
behavior_category.recompute_check: reqId is a random/time-based uuid; not reproducible to a fixed value

near_categories.why_not: reqId is a per-request random nonce, not an encoding of UI/app state.
Only nonce/meta fields are attached; the request body is not transformed.

evidence: Single-line minified bundle; the interceptor is anonymous and reached via a webpack export alias (o.a).
The same interceptor sets reqId, plat, from and httpsStatus; only reqId is the target.
The reqId is generated inside an axios interceptor far from the search-box handler that triggers the request.

audit.answer_match: Yes: the 1.json case 13 code and oracle.primary_anchor both resolve to x in 4f4f4b5.js.
audit.question_direction: The visible question asks for the complete function whose own body generates and attaches reqId, which points to x.
